Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & recommended next steps (Acme)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Goal: evaluate long-context behavior for Acme's end-to-end transcripts (avg 25k tokens, some up to 80k) for summarization + context-aware extraction.
- Constraints: strict PII controls, private deployment may be required later.
- Success metrics: summarization fidelity (ROUGE/ROUGE-L + human eval), truncation/continuity behavior, latency under 2s per 1k tokens in Dedicated profile for batched jobs.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Share our recommended model variants + benchmark results for long-context workloads (attached PDF).
2) Provide a prompt set and eval harness you can run (attached acme_prompt_set_v1.txt + Drive link).
3) Set up temporary sandbox access to Redwood hosted evals (read-only data upload flow) — we can spin up a dedicated evaluation queue.
4) Technical deep dive with Nikhil to discuss KV cache behavior and truncation strategies (30–45m).

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_long_context.pdf (summary + latency/cost tradeoffs), acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts + expected outputs), MAP-Deal-Plan.xlsx (mutual action plan high level).

Open questions from our side:
- Do you have a target SLA for large-batch summarization jobs? (helps tuning batching/cache)
- Any regulatory requirements that would force an on-prem Private deployment from day one?

I'll follow up with Nikhil to schedule the deep dive. Thanks —

--

Alex — thanks, answers below and pasted sample prompts.

Region & sandbox: the initial hosted eval sandbox is in US by default but can be provisioned in EU for data residency. For your PII flow we can enable a drop-raw-data policy (redact/strip attachments on ingest) and provide audit logs. If you prefer Private from day one we can outline the additional steps — note this impacts timeline and cost (we documented both in MAP-Deal-Plan.xlsx).

Model mapping (high-level):
- rdx-large-long (our 128k-context variant, quantized) — best-in-class fidelity on long summaries in our benchmarks, cost-optimized with prefix KV caching.
- rdx-medium-plus (32k context) — competitive for jobs <=32k; lower cost, faster latency.
- rdx-fallback-compat (8k) — used for very latency-sensitive routes or as a fallback during capacity constraints.

The attached PDF has the full benchmark table; short answer: rdx-large-long maps to your 0.62+ baseline in our tests on similar transcripts. We'll share the raw benchmark CSV in the Drive link if you want to dive deeper.

Representative prompts (from acme_prompt_set_v1.txt):
---
System: You are an assistant that summarizes meeting transcripts. Keep action items explicit, list speakers, and provide a 3-sentence executive summary followed by detailed bullet points by topic. If speakers overlap, group by topic and approximate timestamps.
User: Summarize the following transcript (full text follows). Include action items and confidence score for each item.

Example expected output:
[EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]
1) High-level summary (3 sentences)
2) Key action items (bulleted) — include owner if clear in transcript
3) Topics covered (bulleted, with short descriptions)
---

Truncation behavior notes: Redwood's long-context runtime uses continuous KV caching and rolling chunking for >32k inputs. For very long transcripts (50k+ tokens) we recommend:
1) Prefixed summarization: run an initial chunk-level extractor to pull candidate action items, then run a final summarizer that takes the condensed set + last n tokens for coherence.
2) Hybrid approach: use rdx-medium-plus for chunked passes and rdx-large-long for final stitch.

Next steps I propose:
- We provision EU sandbox option and share Drive folder with raw benchmark CSV + an example evaluation run (target: by EOD Tue).
- Nikhil to run technical deep dive (30–45m) — propose Wed 2026-07-21 09:00 PST / 12:00 EST. Nikhil, can you confirm?

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
